diagnostic_evidence.quote: The $BC^1(\R)$-norm is stronger than the norm of the Wiener algebra $A(\R)$, as is implied by \eqref{eq:katz}.
Hence, the $\mathcal{O}(\eps)$ defect bound is also valid in the $A(\R)$-norm.
The proof is based on \eqref{eq:katz} and follows the same steps as the proof in \cite[Lemma 4.2]{shi2025weighted}.

issues.failure_explanation: The second inequality in eq:katz is false on R. For f = sin x, or a constant, f and f' are bounded, but f is not in A(R), since elements of A(R) are inverse Fourier transforms of L^1 functions and so vanish at infinity. Even in C_0 it fails: f_N = sum_{k=1}^N phi(x - kL) with disjoint bumps has bounded f_N and f_N', while ||f_N||_A grows like log N (Dirichlet kernel). The bound holds only under a support restriction or with an H^1 norm. The proof of Prop prop and Lemma lem:defect-wiener use it to pass from BC^1 defect bounds to A(R) bounds. The defects there involve NLS solutions a^+-, b^+-, which do not have bounded support.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace eq:katz by ||f||_A <= c||f||_{H^1(R)}. Strengthen the regularity assumptions on a^+-, b^+-, a, b to Sobolev regularity (L^2-integrable derivatives). Redo the defect estimates in H^1, which then controls the A(R) norm.
issues.overall_effect: The Wiener-algebra defect bounds are unsupported. These are needed for the exact-solution approximations (prop, prop2) and as input to nonlinear stability, so all error bounds lose their justification.
issues.title: False embedding of W^{1,infinity}(R) into the Wiener algebra A(R) in eq:katz
issues.why_classification: The conclusions likely survive. However, a false lemma must be replaced, the hypotheses changed, and the defect estimates redone in a different norm, including the nondecaying-type factors in b^+-. This is more than a local fix but needs no new architecture.

issues.failure_explanation: Prop prop2 gives an O(eps^2) approximation only for (a + eps b) times the phase. Although b(0)=0, b is forced by -2c_g d_t d_xi a and is generically nonzero for t>0. Hence p minus a^+ times the phase equals eps*b times the phase plus O(eps^2), which is O(eps), not O(eps^2). The same holds for q. The O(eps^2) claim in eq:pq is false as stated.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace O(eps^2) by O(eps) in eq:pq, or include eps*b^+- in the definitions of the tilde p and tilde q.
issues.overall_effect: Only the displayed O(eps^2) claim is wrong. eq:upq needs only O(eps) and remains valid.
issues.title: eq:pq claims O(eps^2) accuracy for the leading term without the eps*b correction
issues.why_classification: A one-line correction suffices, and no downstream result uses the O(eps^2) order.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: For polarized initial data, the defect is in fact smaller:
The maximum norm in the defect bound of Lemma~\ref{lem:defect-max} turns out to be too weak a norm for the proof of Theorems~\ref{th:MFE} and~\ref{thm}.

issues.failure_explanation: Nonlinear stability (lem:stability) needs the defect in C([0,T],A(R)), and the paper itself says the maximum norm is too weak. Remark defect-pola asserts, without proof, only an L^infinity bound O(tau^2+h^2+eps^2) for the polarized defect. No A(R)-norm analogue of lem:defect-wiener is stated or proved for the polarized case. The first-step error at the O(eps^2) level is also not estimated. The eps^2 improvement is therefore unsupported.

failure_location.quote: The higher-order accuracy in $\eps$ for the solution $u$ follows from the polarized approximation in Proposition~\ref{prop2} together with the refined defect estimate for the numerical solution given in Remark~\ref{defect-pola}.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State and prove a Wiener-norm defect bound O(tau^2+h^2+eps^2) for the polarized tilde p = (a + eps b) times the phase, following lem:defect-wiener. Add the corresponding estimate for the weighted Euler start step.
issues.overall_effect: The O(tau^2+h^2+eps^2) bounds of thm:polarized for p and v_+ lack a complete proof.
issues.title: Polarized eps^2 bound relies on an unproven max-norm defect estimate where a Wiener-norm estimate is required
issues.why_classification: The missing estimate follows the same routine pattern as the general-case defect lemma. No change to the method, rate, or scope is needed.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: equivalent to the norm $\|\cdot\|_{A(\mathbb{R}) \times A(\mathbb{R})}$ uniformly in $\eps,\tau,h$ subject to \eqref{eq:stability}

issues.failure_explanation: Take the mode theta = beta/h, so beta - theta h = 0. There tilde gamma_theta = 1 and gamma_theta = alpha(1+kappa^2) = alpha omega^2. Hence tilde gamma^2/(1+gamma^2) = 1/(1+alpha^2 omega^4), which tends to 1 as alpha = -tau/(omega eps^2) -> 0. Condition (stability) only bounds |alpha| from above, so no mu<1 independent of eps, tau, h exists. In this limit lambda^+ and lambda^- coalesce, with |lambda^+ - lambda^-| about 2 omega tau/eps^2, so ||V(theta)^{-1}|| grows like eps^2/tau. The claimed uniform equivalence thus fails for tau << eps^2 (e.g. eps=1, tau->0). The CN lemma, which defers to the same procedure, fails identically: there |gamma_theta|^2 = 1 + alpha^2 omega^4 at this mode, so 1/|gamma_theta| -> 1.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace uniform norm equivalence by a theta-wise argument. Show that ||V(theta)^{-1}|| |tau^2/(eps^2(1+i gamma_theta))| <= C tau and that ||V(theta)|| <= 2. Bound the starting term V^{-1}E^0 by a refined first-step error estimate of size O((tau/eps^2)(tau^2+h^2+eps)). Alternatively, restrict to tau >= c0 eps^2 and treat the complementary regime by classical analysis.
issues.overall_effect: Nonlinear stability and hence the error bounds are not shown to have constants independent of tau and eps when tau << eps^2. The advertised uniformity over 0 < eps <= 1, including the O(tau^{2/7}+h^{2/5}) uniform-accuracy remark, is unsupported in that regime.
issues.title: Claimed uniform norm equivalence in linear stability fails as tau/eps^2 -> 0
issues.why_classification: The rate and method likely survive, but the stability lemma as stated is false. Restoring uniformity requires a contained new argument (mode-wise amplification and start-step estimates) or a regime restriction, not just a local fix.
